# Brandon Allan Fluegel, Ph.D. — Human Factors Engineering Portfolio

> Brandon Allan Fluegel, Ph.D., is a Senior Human Factors Design Engineer at Intuitive Surgical. His work focuses on human factors for surgical robotics. He earned his Ph.D. in Human Factors Psychology at Old Dominion University. His portfolio documents prior research and engineering projects at Amazon Devices, NASA, and Mercedes-Benz. He authored a human-AI trust audit framework and is a co-inventor of a U.S. patent.

Portfolio release: v3.0.0 (Winter 2026)
Last reviewed: 2026-11-22

## Profile
- **Current role:** Senior Human Factors Design Engineer at Intuitive Surgical.
- **Education:** Ph.D. in Human Factors Psychology, Old Dominion University.
- **Prior project roles:** Human Factors Researcher in Amazon Devices Design Group; Human Factors Ph.D. intern projects at NASA and Mercedes-Benz.
- **Focus areas:** Human factors engineering, surgical robotics, human-machine interaction, simulated-use validation, psychophysics, cognitive workload, and Human-AI interaction.

## Selected work
- **Amazon Devices:** Led Alexa response-latency research across 20,000+ trials and identified a 1,000 ms High Satisfaction Threshold. Alexa Economics projected $50M in incremental operational value over 15 months if latency targets were met; this was a projection, not realized value. Separate fNIRS and eye-tracking research informed Echo Show and Echo Hub products serving 75M+ active customers; 75M+ is product reach, not study-participant count. Co-inventor of US Patent 12,532,040 B1 and recipient of the 2023 Amazon Inventor Award.
- **NASA Lunar Gateway:** Human factors validation of a medical workstation under simulated microgravity reduced time-on-task for complex medical procedures by 30% versus baseline.
- **Mercedes-Benz:** Semi-autonomous driving interface and psychoacoustic research. Structured evaluations reported 15% lower perceived cabin noise and a 24% increase in driver trust scores during automated lane changes and handoffs.
- **Human-AI trust:** Authored a four-phase, six-principle audit framework for non-deterministic interfaces.
